prompt: explain quantum entaglement like I'm five
response:
Okay, let's imagine you have a special pair of magic gloves. These gloves are so special that whatever you do with one glove, the other glove does the exact same thing, no matter how far apart they are!

For example, if you turn one glove inside out, the other glove will also turn inside out at the same time, even if it's all the way across the world. This happens instantly, as if the gloves can talk to each other without using any phones or messages.

In the world of very tiny things, like atoms and particles, some of them can be "quantum entangled" just like these magic gloves. When two particles are entangled, whatever happens to one particle happens to the other, no matter how far apart they are. It's like they're connected by an invisible, magical thread that lets them know what's happening to each other right away!
